description: Cryptographic assets used by credo-openbao-kms. scripts/generate-cbom.mjs turns this inventory into a CycloneDX 1.6 CBOM and verifies that every 'detect' pattern still exists in the source.

openbao.name: OpenBao (Transit and KV v2)
openbao.description: OpenBao server providing the Transit secrets engine and the KV v2 fallback mount used by this package. Version 2.7.2 is the version verified by the live check.

node-crypto.name: Node.js crypto (OpenSSL)
node-crypto.description: Node.js built-in crypto module backed by the bundled OpenSSL. Used for key generation, verification, PKCS#8/JWK conversion, AES-ECB (inside AES-KWP), RSA-OAEP and hashing.

noble-curves.name: @noble/curves
noble-curves.description: Pure-JavaScript secp256k1 implementation used for key generation, signing and verification when the runtime's OpenSSL build does not support the curve.

assets.name: Ed25519
assets.description: Edwards-curve signature algorithm used for EdDSA keys and DID documents. Keys are generated and used inside OpenBao Transit; signatures are verified locally with node:crypto.

assets.name: ECDSA P-256
assets.description: NIST P-256 ECDSA signatures used for ES256 and DID keys. Generated and used inside OpenBao Transit; signatures are verified locally with node:crypto.

assets.name: ECDSA P-384
assets.description: NIST P-384 ECDSA signatures used for ES384 and DID keys. Generated and used inside OpenBao Transit; signatures are verified locally with node:crypto.

assets.name: ECDSA P-521
assets.description: NIST P-521 ECDSA signatures used for ES512 and DID keys. Generated and used inside OpenBao Transit; signatures are verified locally with node:crypto.

assets.name: secp256k1 ECDSA
assets.description: secp256k1 (ES256K) signatures for did:key, did:jwk and did:peer. Transit cannot represent this curve, so keys are stored in OpenBao KV v2 and signed in-process with @noble/curves.

assets.name: X25519
assets.description: Curve25519 Diffie-Hellman key type used for DID key agreement. Transit cannot represent it, so key pairs are generated with node:crypto and stored in OpenBao KV v2. Credo 0.7 does not expose a key-agreement operation to this backend.

assets.name: RSA-2048 (PKCS#1 v1.5)
assets.description: RSA-2048 signatures used for RS256/RS384/RS512 and X.509 chains. Keys are generated, imported and used inside OpenBao Transit; signatures are verified locally with node:crypto.

assets.name: RSA-3072 (PKCS#1 v1.5)
assets.description: RSA-3072 signatures used for RS256/RS384/RS512 and X.509 chains. Keys are generated, imported and used inside OpenBao Transit; signatures are verified locally with node:crypto.

assets.name: RSA-4096 (PKCS#1 v1.5)
assets.description: RSA-4096 signatures used for RS256/RS384/RS512 and X.509 chains. Keys are generated, imported and used inside OpenBao Transit; signatures are verified locally with node:crypto.

assets.name: RSASSA-PSS (RSA-2048/3072/4096)
assets.description: RSA-PSS signatures used for PS256/PS384/PS512. The backend sets salt_length=hash so JWA-compliant verifiers accept the signatures.

properties.name: credo:crypto:padding
properties.value: RSASSA-PSS, salt length equal to the hash length

assets.name: RSA-OAEP-256 (RSA-4096)
assets.description: RSA-OAEP with SHA-256 and MGF1-SHA-256 used to wrap the ephemeral AES key during Transit BYOK import. The wrapping key is always the server's RSA-4096 key.

assets.name: AES-256 Key Wrap with Padding (RFC 5649)
assets.description: AES Key Wrap with Padding used to wrap PKCS#8 private key material for Transit BYOK import. Implemented in src/aesKeyWrap.ts and unwrapped by OpenBao Transit.

assets.name: AES-256-ECB
assets.description: Single-block AES-ECB primitives used internally by the RFC 5649 AES-KWP implementation. No application data is encrypted directly with ECB.

assets.name: SHA-256
assets.description: SHA-256 digest used by ES256, RS256, PS256, ES256K, RSA-OAEP and MGF1. Computed locally with node:crypto or inside Transit for signing.

assets.name: SHA-384
assets.description: SHA-384 digest used by ES384, RS384 and PS384.

assets.name: SHA-512
assets.description: SHA-512 digest used by ES512, RS512 and PS512.

assets.name: Cryptographically secure random number generation
assets.description: Random bytes for ephemeral AES keys, secp256k1 secret keys and X25519 key generation. Provided by the Node.js OpenSSL CSPRNG (randomBytes) and @noble/curves randomSecretKey.

assets.name: TLS 1.2 / 1.3
assets.description: Transport security for the OpenBao HTTP API. The protocol version and cipher suites are configured on the OpenBao listener; this package requires an https:// address for non-local deployments.

assets.name: OpenBao Transit asymmetric signing keys
assets.description: Private keys created or imported into the Transit secrets engine. For createKey the private key never leaves OpenBao; importKey transfers it once as a wrapped PKCS#8 blob.

securedBy.mechanism: OpenBao barrier encryption and Transit key isolation

assets.name: OpenBao Transit RSA wrapping key
assets.description: The server's RSA-4096 public key returned by GET /transit/wrapping_key and used to wrap the ephemeral AES key for BYOK import.

assets.name: secp256k1 private JWK in OpenBao KV v2
assets.description: Private secp256k1 JWK stored in the configured KV v2 mount when Transit cannot represent the curve. The private key is read into the agent process to sign.

securedBy.mechanism: OpenBao KV v2 barrier encryption; readable by any client with read access to the path

assets.name: X25519 private JWK in OpenBao KV v2
assets.description: Private X25519 JWK stored in the configured KV v2 mount when Transit cannot represent the curve. Used for DID key agreement by the Credo agent.

securedBy.mechanism: OpenBao KV v2 barrier encryption; readable by any client with read access to the path

assets.name: Ephemeral AES-256 key-encryption key
assets.description: A random 32-byte AES key created for each Transit BYOK import. It wraps the PKCS#8 private key with AES-KWP and is itself wrapped with the Transit RSA wrapping key.

driftWatch.reason: OpenBao's HMAC key type is declared in the client type union but this backend does not implement HMAC operations.
OpenBao AES-GCM and ChaCha20 transit key types are declared in the client type union but are not used by this backend. DIDComm encryption is left to the Node.js/Askar backend.
Only AES-256 is used by the RFC 5649 implementation. Add an inventory asset if AES-128 or AES-192 is introduced.
Weak or unused digest. OpenBao's import API accepts SHA1/SHA224 hash names, but this backend always uses SHA-256.
Curve is not used by Credo 0.7 or this backend.
RSA keys smaller than 2048 bits are not supported by this backend.
Post-quantum algorithm. Add a cryptographic asset before using it.
Password hashing/KDF is not used by this backend.
